description: qou-cds1: the four determinations of the Markov parameter z, each priced against the CAL-1/2/3 CODATA-2022 published uncertainties by recomputing both ends of every gap together (so the q0 correlation survives). The mass channel does NOT confirm the derived cap -- the quoted 0.0203 % is 9.49 sigma -- and that 9.49 is the mu-p substrate tension and the c_3 cross-anchor swing in different coordinates: three corpus facts, one measurement. c_2 = -1 is a 1.6-sigma empirical statement at z_C (not a theorem, and not a 1.76 % miss) and is excluded at 773 sigma under D. Solving implied-c_2 = -1 for z gives a FOURTH determination, 0.499110 +- 0.000132, which is 1.60 sigma from z_C and 863 sigma from the cap: the ladder's anchor independently measures z and selects C. Hence there is no D-frame anchor and the ladder's FORM must change, not its parameter. Scope-(a); nothing derived, wired or readmitted.

assertions.name: control_reproduces_the_committed_determinations
assertions.detail: cap and mass to 1e-15 through the imported symbolic trace; decay to 1.49e-8 (F reconstructed, not re-derived — stated as a tolerance)

assertions.name: mass_channel_does_not_confirm_the_cap
assertions.detail: the quoted '0.0203 %' is 9.49479 sigma. Far closer than decay and still a decisive disagreement; 'mass puts z essentially where the cap does' does not survive its own bar

assertions.name: decay_channel_is_excluded_by_five_orders_of_sigma
assertions.detail: 888508.0 sigma — the decay anomaly is real and is not a leverage artefact

assertions.name: mu_p_tension_and_mass_cap_gap_are_one_measurement
assertions.detail: 9.49362 vs 9.49479 sigma, agreeing to 0.0123 % — same quantity in two coordinates, and the c_3 swing is a third

assertions.name: c2_equals_minus_one_is_a_low_sigma_C_frame_statement
assertions.detail: implied c_2 at z_C = -1.0145717 +- 0.006695, i.e. 2.176 sigma from -1: agreement, not a 1.76 % miss — and empirical, not proved

assertions.name: c2_equals_minus_one_is_excluded_under_D
assertions.detail: implied c_2 at z_D = -9.29581191, 1239.79 sigma from -1 — THERE IS NO D-FRAME ANCHOR at c_2 = -1

assertions.name: ladder_anchor_is_a_measurement_of_z_and_selects_C
assertions.detail: z from implied-c_2 = -1 is 0.499141856 +- 8.2e-5: 2.177 sigma from z_C, 1384.83 sigma from the derived cap

assertions.name: two_decay_side_functionals_disagree_beyond_the_K_wall
assertions.detail: trace reduction z = 0.998500317 vs ladder z = 0.499141856; reconciling needs K off by 2.2654426x, 20.05x outside the 6.31 % parameter-free wall

context.axis: qou-cds1 anchor side: does a D-frame ladder anchor exist?
context.answer: NO. c_2 = -1 is supported at 1.6 sigma under C and excluded at 773 sigma under D, and the ladder anchor read as a measurement of z lands 1.60 sigma from z_C and 863 sigma from the derived cap. The C->D move cannot be completed by finding a D-frame c_2; the ladder's functional FORM has to change. This is the anchor-side statement of what decayLadder_zC_threeRow_ne_zero says structurally.
context.corrects: the standing reading that mass 'essentially confirms' the cap and so localises the anomaly to decay: mass-vs-cap is 9.49 sigma. Both channels disagree with the derived cap; decay disagrees 5.8e4 times harder.
context.scope: Scope-(a). Nothing derived, proposed, wired or readmitted; no convention adjudicated; no c_k value changed. A z landing near an inadmissible point is TENSION, not permission -- one_not_root stands, as does the derived two-row cap.
